title: Uninitialized Members and Padding Information Leak
platform_conditions: C++11 and later on any conforming toolchain; padding layout follows the platform ABI (Itanium/SysV, MSVC)
security_mechanism: A class with no default member initializers leaves its members indeterminate when default-constructed on the stack or via a raw allocation: reading a field yields whatever bytes occupied the storage, which may be a previous request's data. Two consequences follow: logic reading such a field (an authorization flag, a length) behaves attacker-shiftable, and a whole-object serialize — copying sizeof(S) including the ABI padding the compiler inserts between members — transmits uninitialized padding bytes to the peer, leaking fragments of earlier heap or stack contents. C++11 member initializers and value-initialization `S s{}` close the gap; placement-new into raw storage does not.

source_sink_clues.source: Objects constructed on request paths without explicit initialization and then serialized, hashed, or copied into responses; padding bytes covered by whole-object copies.
source_sink_clues.sink: memcpy/send/serialize over sizeof(obj) of a default-constructed object; any read of a member that no constructor initialized

tracking_guards: Check that every member has a default member initializer (`int x{0};`) or the constructor initializes all members, that instances are value-initialized (`S s{};`) rather than default constructed, and that serialization copies field-by-field (or via a member-wise serializer) instead of whole-object memcpy of sizeof(S).
not_candidate_when: Every constructor initializes every member and value-initialization is used at each instantiation, the object is never serialized beyond its explicitly-written fields, or the type is only used as an internal scratch object whose bytes never leave the process.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: struct S { int x; int y; }; S s; serialize(s);
synthetic_safe_example: struct S { int x{0}; int y{0}; }; S s{}; serialize(s);
public_references: C++ Core Guidelines: C.41 (initialize in constructors) — https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines
